name: Smart Went Crazy
label: Dischord
lede: Smart Went Crazy, five DC players with an electric cello, made a 73-minute second album for Dischord, covered Laurie Anderson on it, and split within a year. Chad Clark says he was relieved.

eras.title: Only when school was out
eras.text: Smart Went Crazy existed only between semesters, and its first record came out on a label the band ran itself. Dischord calls it a low-key partnership between Chad Clark, Abram Goodrich and Hilary Soldati.

years.cap: Chad Clark and Hilary Soldati rehearsing in Washington, DC, 1993
years.h: Three friends start a band that only exists on school breaks
years.p: [[Chad Clark|f3f09e99-e31c-4aa2-99e4-0b4e59e72f87]] sings and plays guitar, Abram Goodrich plays bass, Hilary Soldati plays cello. Dischord says they played together only between semesters.
years.xp:
Wikipedia describes the founders as high school students in Washington, DC; Dischord's history doesn't name a school, only the semester breaks.

The cello was not a novelty. It was the third voice in the band from the first rehearsals.

years.h: CozyDisc, the band's own label, puts out Cubbyhole
years.p: The debut EP is a self-release. Dischord comes later, after the trio becomes a full band.

eras.title: Five people and a cello
eras.text: After graduation the trio grew into a full band with a second guitar and a drummer, and landed on Dischord. In a guitar town, what set it apart was Soldati's electric cello, sawing and droning where a lead guitar would usually go.

years.cap: Chad Clark singing, the cello at left, at the Knitting Factory, New York, 1996
years.h: A trio graduates and becomes a quintet
years.p: [[Jeff Boswell|6c40b2b3-cabb-40a2-85d6-ceab52159cd1]] joins on guitar and Tony Dennison on drums, and Soldati's electric cello takes the parts a lead guitar would.
years.xp:
Dischord's history says the band expanded only after its members graduated. The Ernest Jenning reissue notes single out Soldati's electric cello as the band's most distinctive element.

Soldati also played organ on Now We're Even, and sang. Clark wrote and sang most of the songs and would go on to produce the band's records himself.

Clark told Treble the band never placed itself in punk or hardcore: "We just felt sort of separate from that." He also credited Dischord for never handing him aesthetic boundaries.

yt: Now We're Even, full album audio
years.p: Eighteen songs, recorded in summer 1995 with Tony Dennison on drums. Titles run from Best and Final Offer to Garden Variety Hate Song.

years.cap: Chad Clark singing under magenta light, Boston, 1996
years.h: Three US tours follow the first album
years.p: Dischord counts three behind Now We're Even, and the band's first line-up change comes out of that stretch.

years.h: Devin Ocampo takes the drum stool from Tony Dennison
years.p: [[Devin Ocampo|10bc183b-b6a8-4769-9e7a-0637d0f8a7a8]] plays on everything the band does after that, and turns out to be just as good on guitar.

years.h: Live at the Hurricane, Kansas City, August 12, 1996
yt: Live at the Hurricane, Kansas City, August 12, 1996

eras.title: The long record, the short goodbye
eras.text: Con Art was huge on purpose: 18 songs, 73 minutes, produced by Clark and the band at Inner Ear. It sounded almost nothing like the DC punk around it, and the band suspected it was the last one.

years.p: Smart Went Crazy's second album, recorded at Inner Ear Studios and produced by Clark and the band. Eighteen tracks, 73 minutes, from Black Kites to the two-part DC Will Do That To You.
years.xp:
Treble hears it as the record where the band broke from DC punk tradition: cello, space and long quiet stretches instead of volume. It was conceived as a double LP; Clark told Treble they talked about Sandinista! a lot, and "We kind of overshot what the label was comfortable with."

Dischord's own history calls it both an impressive musical document and a portrait of a band falling apart. Clark says the group could feel during the sessions that it would be the last one.

years.cap: Hilary Soldati on electric cello, Portland, 1998
years.h: A Laurie Anderson song turns up on Con Art
years.p: The band covers [[Laurie Anderson|86809b51-cbe2-45f1-804a-e66eed635dea]]'s Let X=X. Not the cover anyone expected from a Dischord band.

yt: Chad Clark interview, Dig Me Out, 2023
years.h: Smart Went Crazy are done less than a year after Con Art
years.p: Clark's word for it, in Treble. Wikipedia puts the split down to internal conflicts among five strong personalities.
years.xp:
Clark told Treble that "I think the band had sensed that it might be our last record." He described five intense, emotional people with strong and conflicting ideas, and said part of the ambition of Con Art was to wring out the band's collective ideas in one record, knowing there wouldn't be another.

His verdict on the afterlife: "the band has become more celebrated in its death than it was celebrated in its life." Dischord's history just says the band dissolved in 1998, shortly after the album came out.

years.h: Ocampo trades drums for guitar, then heads to Faraquet
years.p: Devin Ocampo switches to guitar and vocals and goes on to [[Faraquet|e866e006-4c80-4753-b53f-1bc5d88ccddd]], then [[Medications|c545a7bf-c8d7-4368-8009-22e19d8911ce]], where Jeff Boswell briefly played bass.

eras.title: The record outlives the band
eras.text: Smart Went Crazy stayed broken up, but Con Art kept finding listeners: on critics' lists, among other musicians, and finally on the vinyl it was meant for. Clark built a second act with Beauty Pill and as a producer, through two heart operations.

yt: Chad Clark on The Trap Set, 2020
years.h: Clark and Goodrich start Beauty Pill
years.p: [[Beauty Pill|976b28a1-dd68-4c43-ba08-ba15b58963b2]] begins after Smart Went Crazy dissolves, with Devin Ocampo drumming. Clark also becomes a busy producer and engineer for [[The Dismemberment Plan|1131e5da-dfdf-46c9-b6ff-b7ac552c2a3c]], [[Q and Not U|a934e33f-b3cb-47dd-9638-f7f1f25fe162]], [[Black Eyes|50d90400-e7ea-4465-92a5-404605e51ee7]] and [[Mary Timony|d9c8dc3c-15b8-40d5-8153-ae9214aeef55]].
He develops viral cardiomyopathy in fall 2007 and has the operation in February 2008, Wikipedia reports. In spring 2022 he needs an emergency heart transplant.

years.cap: Con Art, reissued as the double LP it was meant to be
years.h: Twenty years on, Con Art gets its double LP
years.p: Ernest Jenning announces a remastered, vinyl-only double LP from the source tapes: 500 copies on clear vinyl, redesigned by Henry Owings of Chunklet. Dischord distributes it as EJRC143.
years.xp:
The reissue notes call it an underground classic whose stature grew with time, and point to Pitchfork putting it on its list of the best albums of the 1990s.

Clark wrote the liner notes during the remastering session. He told Treble some of it is "a little embarrassing, kind of like baby pictures", and that he's "made more money from Con Art because it's influential on other musicians" than from royalties.
